topStories.headline: Castro Theatre's Revived Era Draws Crowds Five Months After $41 Million Reopening
topStories.dek: The historic Castro Theatre, now under Another Planet Entertainment's management, has been operating as a full-scale live-events venue since February — and the summer calendar is packed.
topStories.body:
Five months after reopening its doors following a two-year closure and a $41 million renovation, the Castro Theatre continues to be the focal point of the neighborhood's cultural renaissance. The century-old landmark officially reopened on February 6, 2026, with a sold-out community fundraiser for the Castro Community Benefit District that featured a 35mm screening of cult classic 'The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert.' The reopening drew city leaders and notable community figures to celebrate the venue's return.

New owners Another Planet Entertainment — who operate several Bay Area venues — reconfigured the 1,400-seat theater to allow for flexible seating, enabling the space to host concerts, comedy shows, drag performances, and film screenings. The controversial renovation, which eliminated the sloped fixed seating that preservationists had fought to protect, cost $41 million and included a restored decorative ceiling, a new digital organ, and updated acoustics, bathrooms, and ADA accessibility improvements.

The summer lineup has included major acts across genres, with upcoming shows through fall 2026. The theatre's booking strategy reflects its new multi-use identity: The Breeders are scheduled for August 22, followed by Melanie C on September 22. The Frameline Film Festival returned to the Castro in June for its 50th anniversary, signaling that the venue's LGBTQ+ cultural programming remains intact alongside the new concert model.

Not all neighbors have embraced the change. Preservation advocates argued that replacing the sloped seating altered the essential character of the filmgoing experience, and some longtime patrons have expressed disappointment that classic and queer film repertory screenings play a smaller role in the new programming mix. The renovation also displaced several Castro-area tenants. Nonetheless, the reopened venue has brought significant foot traffic back to 18th and Castro, and local merchants say they hope the continued programming will sustain a broader neighborhood revival.

topStories.headline: Glen Park Wins Over $65,000 in Avenue Greenlight Grants for Neighborhood Improvements
topStories.dek: Three separate grants will fund murals, planters, beautification of the Pono patio, and new neighborhood banners along Mission Street.
topStories.body:
Glen Park has secured more than $65,000 in Avenue Greenlight grant funding this year, with three separate awards targeting visible, community-driven improvements to the neighborhood's commercial corridors and public spaces. The grants were announced at the Glen Park Association's Summer 2026 Quarterly Meeting, held July 16 at Bird & Beckett Books & Records on Chenery Street.

The three projects funded by the grants include: corner murals and planters along Slow Arlington Street, beautification of the Pono patio — which the association says could become a pop-up events site in the future — and new neighborhood banners along Mission Street between Highland and Bosworth, the gateway corridor into Glen Park. The banner project connects the neighborhood's identity along a stretch where newer businesses like EvolvedSF and Keikos Coffee Shop have joined long-standing establishments.

The Slow Arlington improvements build on an earlier Avenue Greenlight-funded effort. In a prior round, the Glen Park Association used a $25,000 grant to take advantage of SFMTA's Community Corners program, installing planters and refreshed Slow Street signage. About 30 neighbors came out in May to help create signs and planters along the street, which serves as a 'bike bus' route for children attending Dolores Huerta and Glen Park elementary schools.

Avenue Greenlight is a philanthropically funded initiative that deploys privately resourced dollars to support community improvement projects in San Francisco's commercial corridors. Upcoming neighborhood events connected to this momentum include the August 1 Greenway Work Day, the August 15 Glen Park Night Market on Kern Street, and a block party on Slow Arlington on August 29.

topStories.headline: GLBT Historical Society Plans New Permanent Museum at 2280 Market Street in Castro
topStories.dek: The city finalized the purchase of 2280 Market Street in late 2024, and designers are now being engaged for the expanded LGBTQ+ cultural institution.
topStories.body:
The GLBT Historical Society is moving forward with plans to establish a permanent, expanded home at 2280 Market Street in the heart of the Castro, after the City and County of San Francisco finalized the property purchase in November 2024. The city and state have committed $18 million to acquire and renovate the site, which will become the permanent home of the nation's first full-scale, stand-alone museum dedicated to LGBTQ+ history and culture.

The new location off Market and Noe Streets is described by the Historical Society as more than eight times larger than the current 1,660-square-foot museum space at 4127 18th Street — enough room to display significantly more of the organization's vast archival holdings and to host large-scale programming. The organization plans to begin designing the space in 2026, working with the community to define needs before the renovation gets underway.

Founded in 1985, the GLBT Historical Society maintains one of the world's largest collections of LGBTQ archival materials. The current museum, open since 2011, is often described as San Francisco's 'queer Smithsonian.' The organization plans to remain at its 18th Street location until renovations at the new site are complete. A capital campaign to raise additional renovation funds is expected to be launched.

The expansion plans reflect a broader vision for Castro's cultural infrastructure. The new facility is intended to serve as a full-scale museum, archives, and research center — a major upgrade from the current intimate space that has long been celebrated for punching above its weight. City officials including District 8 Supervisor Rafael Mandelman have championed the project as central to preserving the Castro's identity as a living monument to LGBTQ+ history.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.location: Noe Valley Town Square, 3862 24th St at Sanchez St, Noe Valley
events.description: Free monthly outdoor market featuring live music, local food and retail vendors, and family-friendly fun at the Noe Valley Town Square. Held the last Tuesday of most months, 5–8 PM.

events.title: Castro Art Walk — First Friday

events.title: Glen Park Night Market
events.location: Kern Street at Diamond Street (+ parking lot), Glen Park
events.description: The third of four free summer night markets on Kern Street, featuring local artists and makers, live music and DJ sets, neighborhood food vendors, and a kids' activity area; runs until 8:30 PM and is presented by the Glen Park Association, Glen Park Merchants Association, and Art Walk SF.

events.title: Castro Art Mart — First Sunday
events.location: Noe Street between Market and Beaver Streets, Castro
events.description: Free monthly LGBTQ+ open-air market featuring dozens of local artists, makers, musicians, and drag performers taking over Noe Street; runs until 8 PM and is hosted by ArtyHood and Castro Merchants.

events.title: Castro Night Market — August Edition
events.description: The monthly Castro Night Market returns for its August installment, filling two blocks of 18th Street with local food vendors, merchants, and live entertainment; free, non-alcoholic, and open to all, running until 10 PM.

events.title: Castro Carnival Family Block Party
events.location: Noe Street at Market Street, Castro
events.description: Free, family-friendly Carnival block party hosted by Castro Merchants, featuring LGBTQ+ artists, live music, and drag performances in the heart of the Castro; runs noon to 5 PM.

events.title: Weekly Jazz at Bird & Beckett
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery St, Glen Park
events.description: Glen Park's beloved bookshop-performance venue hosts jazz, blues, and poetry events nearly every week: 'Jazz in the Bookshop' every Friday at 5:30 PM, Saturday night 'Jazz Club' at 7:30 PM, and 'Which Way West?' concerts on select days — all with modest suggested donations.

events.title: Castro Farmers Market
events.location: Noe Street at Market & Beaver, Castro
events.description: The weekly Castro Farmers Market runs every Wednesday from 3–7 PM on Noe Street through October, offering fresh produce, artisan goods, and local food vendors in the heart of the neighborhood.

moreNews.headline: New Businesses Continue to Fill Castro Storefronts as Neighborhood Rebounds
moreNews.body: A wave of new businesses has been opening along Castro Street and Market Street in 2026, adding to the sense of revival that followed the Castro Theatre's February reopening. Among the recent arrivals is Antoine's Cookie Shop, which opened its first San Francisco location at 2073 Market Street. Proprietor Antoine Tang, who has three other Bay Area locations, brings a cookie brand known in part for its snickerdoodle, which appeared in a 2021 advertisement featuring Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry. Local business leaders have expressed optimism that the combination of new retail, the active night market series, and the reopened Castro Theatre will help sustain foot traffic and attract further investment to the corridor.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Association Meets at Bird & Beckett, Eyes Transit and Safety Upgrades
moreNews.body: The Glen Park Association held its Summer 2026 Quarterly Meeting on July 16 at Bird & Beckett Books & Records on Chenery Street, where representatives from the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency presented updates on upcoming neighborhood projects. Safety improvements discussed included flashing beacons for pedestrians crossing Bosworth at Brompton, a larger stop sign on Chenery at Elk, and crosswalk improvements — changes the GPA credited to sustained community input. The meeting also previewed changes to the 35 and 36 bus lines affecting the area, with updated service substitution information available on the SFMTA website.

moreNews.headline: Fabulosa Books Carries on Castro Literary Tradition at 489 Castro Street
moreNews.body: Fabulosa Books, the LGBTQ+-focused independent bookstore at 489 Castro Street, continues to serve as a literary anchor for the neighborhood following its rebranding from Dog Eared Books Castro in 2021. Owner Alvin Orloff, who spent 21 years managing Dog Eared Books before purchasing the Castro location on his 60th birthday, has built the store into a multi-award-winning community institution — the Bay Area Reporter named it 'Favorite Bookstore' three years in a row. The shop carries LGBTQ+ literature and related materials alongside general selections, and hosts ongoing community programming including book clubs and readings.

moreNews.headline: Noe Valley Housing Market Stays Competitive Heading into Summer
moreNews.body: Noe Valley's residential real estate market remains tight as the summer progresses, according to recent sales data. In the two-week period ending July 14, 2026, five homes sold in the neighborhood with prices ranging from $695,000 to $3,815,805. Earlier in the year, a two-week snapshot in mid-June showed 14 homes sold with a median price per square foot of $1,281.83 and a median days-on-market of 19. Industry observers note that buyer demand remains strong despite the constrained inventory typical of summer.
moreNews.sourceName: Pacific Edge SF Real Estate Blog

restaurants.name: Catch

restaurants.name: L'Ardoise

restaurants.name: Blind Butcher

restaurants.name: Bacco

restaurants.name: Firefly

restaurants.name: Little Chihuahua
restaurants.description: Noe Valley neighborhood favorite serving fresh, high-quality Mexican food including burritos, tacos, and enchiladas with locally sourced ingredients.

restaurants.name: Haystack Pizza

restaurants.name: Fable
restaurants.description: Castro restaurant praised for excellent ambiance and a creative New American menu using seasonal, locally sourced ingredients.

restaurants.name: Beit Rima
restaurants.description: Acclaimed neighborhood restaurant near Noe Valley offering Palestinian-inspired dishes with exceptional dips, handmade bread, and vibrant flavors.

restaurants.name: Antoine's Cookie Shop

restaurants.name: Café Mystique
restaurants.description: Cozy Castro café known for its strong coffee, welcoming atmosphere, and reliable service, popular with neighborhood regulars.

restaurants.name: The Dubliner

restaurants.name: Glen Park Station

hotels.description: Welcoming boutique hotel in the heart of the Castro District, ideally located for exploring the neighborhood's bars, restaurants, and LGBTQ+ cultural sites.

hotels.name: Noe's Nest Bed and Breakfast
hotels.description: Charming, highly rated 3.5-star B&B nestled in Noe Valley offering cozy pet-friendly rooms, a peaceful atmosphere, and a healthy breakfast.

hotels.name: Beck's Motor Lodge
hotels.description: A classic motor lodge near the Castro offering clean, comfortable rooms with easy access to public transportation and neighborhood dining.

hotels.name: Dolores Place
hotels.description: Intimate bed and breakfast just steps from Mission Dolores Park, well positioned for guests exploring both the Castro and Noe Valley neighborhoods.

hotels.name: Twin Peaks Hotel
hotels.description: Affordable 60-room hotel centrally located near Castro and Twin Peaks, offering straightforward accommodations and easy access to Muni transit.

shops.name: Noe Valley Books
shops.description: Intimate independent bookstore on 24th Street serving the Noe Valley community with a curated selection of titles.

shops.name: Cliff's Variety
shops.description: A Castro landmark since 1936, Cliff's carries an eclectic mix of hardware, housewares, costumes, seasonal decorations, and specialty items beloved by generations of neighbors.

shops.name: Chartreuse by Roje
shops.description: Castro boutique offering unique and stylish apparel and accessories, also a participating venue in the monthly Castro Art Walk.

shops.name: Queer Arts Featured
shops.description: Gallery and retail space at the former site of Harvey Milk's camera shop, showcasing and selling LGBTQ+ artwork and a Castro Art Walk anchor venue.

shops.name: Welcome Castro
shops.description: Castro boutique offering a variety of locally made products including clothing, accessories, and home goods, with a focus on celebrating the neighborhood's identity.

shops.name: Noe Valley Bakery
shops.description: Beloved neighborhood bakery on 24th Street known for exceptional breads, cakes, pastries, and custom decorated cakes for special occasions.

shops.name: EvolvedSF

shops.name: Harvest Urban Market

shops.name: Canyon Market

artEntertainment.name: Castro Theatre
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's iconic 1922 movie palace, reopened in February 2026 after a $41 million renovation by Another Planet Entertainment, now hosting concerts, comedy, drag shows, and film screenings in a flexible 1,400-seat configuration.

artEntertainment.name: GLBT Historical Society Museum
artEntertainment.description: The nation's first full-scale stand-alone museum of LGBTQ+ history and culture, featuring the long-term exhibition 'Queer Past Becomes Present' and rotating programming; open Tuesday–Sunday, admission $10.

artEntertainment.name: MAG Galleries
artEntertainment.description: Castro art gallery at 3931 18th Street serving as a founding anchor of the monthly Castro Art Walk and showcasing works by local and regional artists.

artEntertainment.name: The Artists' Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Castro gallery at 4406 18th Street participating in the monthly Art Walk and offering an ongoing showcase of works by local artists.

artEntertainment.name: Roxie Theater

artEntertainment.name: Harvey Milk Plaza & Rainbow Honor Walk

artEntertainment.name: Glen Park Branch Library
artEntertainment.description: Welcoming neighborhood library in Glen Park hosting a regular schedule of author talks, community programs, and cultural events throughout the year.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF Castro

gymsRecreation.name: Barry's Castro

gymsRecreation.description: Noe Valley's beloved community gathering space — the only neighborhood town square in San Francisco — hosting the monthly Saturday Farmers Market, Night Markets, free classes, and year-round community events.

gymsRecreation.description: Community park and recreation center in upper Noe Valley with a baseball diamond, playground, community garden, and year-round programming for residents of all ages.
